content.user_title: Optimize Vercel Costs and Route Performance
content.value_statement: Vercel bills and slow routes can be difficult to connect to specific code changes. This skill combines production signals and targeted verification to prioritize recommendations.
actual_capabilities: Collect Vercel metrics, usage, contract information, and project settings within a consistent account scope and shared 14-day metric window.
Apply deterministic gates to select routes, files, and platform settings for targeted investigation.
Map observed routes to source files and use supplementary scanners for caching, images, middleware, and build configuration.
Collect focused follow-up metrics and reconcile unsupported optimization hypotheses into observations or no-change findings.
Verify file references, source patterns, cache-safety claims, and framework-version compatibility against a curated citation library.
Render ranked Markdown reports with recommendations, investigation observations, and candidates not investigated during the run.
limitations: Requires a deployed, linked Vercel project, an authenticated Vercel CLI v53+ session, and Node.js 20+.
Route-level analysis requires Observability Plus and meaningful traffic; limited audits require explicit approval.
Next.js, SvelteKit, and Nuxt have stronger support; Astro support is limited, and unsupported frameworks require approval.
Produces recommendations, not automatic deployments, guaranteed performance gains, or precise savings forecasts.

use_cases.title: Investigate a Growing Vercel Bill
use_cases.description: Connect major billing categories to observed route traffic and prioritize supported opportunities to reduce waste.

use_cases.title: Diagnose Slow Application Routes
use_cases.description: Investigate high-latency routes using follow-up metrics, mapped source files, and framework-compatible recommendations.

use_cases.title: Review Content Delivery Efficiency
use_cases.description: Assess caching, image optimization, and regeneration opportunities on a deployed documentation or publishing site.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Vercel Audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this linked Vercel project for cost and performance opportunities. Check prerequisites and collect production signals before investigating source files.

prompt_templates.title: Investigate Function Invocations
prompt_templates.prompt: Investigate function invocation costs in this Vercel project. Use observed traffic to identify candidates and verify caching safety before recommending changes.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze Slow Routes
prompt_templates.prompt: Investigate slow routes using the shared 14-day metric window. Reconcile follow-up evidence and recommend only changes supported by source files and compatible documentation.

prompt_templates.title: Expand a Scoped Audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this Vercel monorepo with up to 12 candidates. Confirm project scope, inspect mapped workspace imports, and report withheld recommendations and evidence gaps.

output_examples.input: Audit a deployed documentation site for unnecessary function invocations.
output: Illustrative result: A frequently requested public documentation route qualifies for a caching investigation.
Recommendation: Cache only verified public content, using a freshness policy compatible with the installed framework version.
The report includes observed traffic, verified file references, citations, and candidates not investigated.
Illustrative result: Long connection duration alone does not establish an optimization opportunity.
Investigation checks active CPU, work before the first response byte, and duplicate invocations.
No change is recommended when available metrics and source files do not support a specific improvement.

output: Illustrative result: Route-level analysis is paused because Observability Plus data is unavailable.
The workflow requests a choice between enabling metrics and accepting a limited audit.
A limited report identifies evidence gaps and avoids unsupported route rankings.

best_practices: Confirm the linked project and team or personal scope before collecting metrics and usage.
Use a fresh run directory and preserve separate standard output and error logs.
Review verified recommendations and cache-safety requirements before implementing changes or deploying.
anti_patterns: Investigating arbitrary source files before production signals select relevant candidates.
Caching authenticated, personalized, error, or fallback responses without evidence that sharing is safe.
Claiming exact savings or recommending framework features unavailable in the installed version.

faq.question: Which projects are suitable?
faq.answer: Use this skill for deployed Vercel projects with meaningful traffic. It is not intended for other hosts or greenfield projects without traffic.

faq.question: Which prerequisites are required?
faq.answer: Use Node.js 20+, Vercel CLI v53+, an authenticated CLI session, and a linked project directory with a resolvable account scope.

faq.question: Is Observability Plus required?
faq.answer: Yes, for route-level metric analysis. If access is unavailable, the workflow asks before continuing with a limited audit.

faq.question: Which frameworks are supported?
faq.answer: Next.js App Router, Next.js Pages Router, SvelteKit, and Nuxt are supported. Astro support is limited; unsupported frameworks require approval for limited analysis.

faq.question: Does the skill apply changes automatically?
faq.answer: The documented workflow produces verified recommendations and a Markdown report. It does not automatically implement changes or deploy the project.

faq.question: Can it guarantee a lower bill?
faq.answer: No. Recommendations depend on observed traffic, available billing signals, and verified source behavior; projected savings use magnitude descriptions rather than exact amounts.
